LHX.sentence: L3Harris ticked up today, but it's been left behind while the four bigger defense contractors rallied hard over the past month — nothing's wrong with the business, it just hasn't caught up yet.

ASML.sentence: ASML keeps climbing, and while it looks expensive on today's earnings, that's because everyone expects a big rebound in chip-machine orders next year.

LIN.sentence: Linde is having a quiet week — steady industrial gas demand under long-term contracts, and it's priced unusually close to its European rival right now.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is quiet, though it's been the standout among the big tech names lately — the AI cloud story keeps grinding along, maybe a little ahead of itself.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher dipped slightly, but biotech funding is thawing, and since that money eventually turns into lab-equipment orders, it's an encouraging sign a couple quarters out.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge dipped slightly and its dividend, while generous, is skinnier than usual compared to safer bonds — so it's looking a bit richly priced, which is why the plan is to trim a little.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow jumped today but sits far below its high from the past year, which is an unusually deep pullback for a company whose corporate AI-automation contracts keep growing.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore was flat while copper prices jumped, so the miner hasn't yet caught up to the metal it digs out of the ground — often a sign it could follow.

RDDT.sentence: Reddit rose today, and its advertising sales are still growing over 60% a year, yet the stock is priced cheaply because investors worry Google could send it fewer visitors.

KOF.sentence: The Latin American Coca-Cola bottler is having a good day and looks inexpensive, with a stable Mexican peso helping the picture.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras drifted down, and its very cheap-looking price is actually a warning that oil earnings may be near their peak, which tempers the optimism.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the container-shipping giant, drifted down and is now trading below the value of its own ships — a floor of sorts, since you couldn't rebuild that fleet for what the stock says it's worth.

MA.sentence: Mastercard was essentially flat, and it's priced unusually close to Visa right now even though it tends to grow a bit faster — every tap of a card still earns it a tiny toll.

ISRG.sentence: The da Vinci surgical robot maker fell again while rival medical-device stocks rose — this looks like a story-driven selloff rather than any real trouble with surgeries or supplies.
